children: ) is on pace to finish the week up roughly 3.9%, extending a stretch of unusually large weekly swings that has now reached four consecutive weeks.
If the current gain holds through the close, the index will have produced moves of at least 2.5% in either direction for a fourth straight week—the longest such run since the 2022 bear market.

The sequence has been pronounced. Two weeks before last week’s sharp decline, the S&P 500 fell -2.7% and then advanced +2.5%. That rebound was followed by an -8.6% drop last week, one of the steepest weekly losses in recent years, before this week’s recovery. The pattern has kept volatility elevated heading into the end of the trading week.

Historical comparisons underscore how uncommon the streak is. It matches four-week runs recorded during the 2020 sell-off and the decline that followed the Dot-com bust in 2000. The longest comparable stretch on record lasted ten weeks amid the 2008 financial crisis.

While past episodes have often occurred during periods of broader market stress, the present sequence has developed against a backdrop of rapid directional reversals rather than a sustained one-way trend. For participants navigating these conditions, the repeated large weekly moves continue to create an exceptional opportunity to respond to short-term dislocations while monitoring the durability of the current recovery.

title: S&P 500 heads for fourth straight week of outsized moves as volatility persists
